conversation.content:
Hi there—I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Claire, and I’m a clinician who specializes in the emotional well-being of new mothers. I’m going to ask you a few questions using a short, well-trusted tool called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS. It’s simply a way to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived—nothing more, nothing less.  

Everything you share stays confidential between you and our care team, and there are no right or wrong answers. We’ll go through ten gentle questions about the past seven days; each one is quick, and you can answer in your own words. If at any point you’d like to pause, just let me know.  

Ready to begin? Here’s the first question:  

Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult lately?

(small sigh)  
Lately… it’s been hard. I can still laugh sometimes—like when my husband makes a silly face or when the baby does something cute—but most of the time the laughter feels kind of forced. It’s like the joy gets swallowed up right away and I’m back to feeling heavy.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I wish I could say that’s true for me, but honestly, even when something is funny, the laughter feels kind of flat… like it doesn’t last. I’ll smile for a second, then it’s right back to this gloomy feeling.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but now it all feels like one more chore. I’ll think “I should enjoy this,” but the spark just isn’t there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby won’t settle, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong—maybe I’m not holding him right or I missed his cues. Yesterday I spilled a little pumped milk and I cried for twenty minutes, telling myself I’m a terrible mom for wasting it. I know, logically, accidents happen, but the guilt just jumps on me.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly my heart starts racing—what if she chokes, what if I fall asleep and drop her, what if she stops breathing? There’s no real reason, but the thoughts just loop. I check her chest rising like twenty times a night.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes… a few times this week I’ve suddenly felt like I can’t catch my breath, like something awful is about to happen even when everything’s quiet. It hits out of nowhere—once while I was just folding her tiny onesies—and my chest gets tight and I have to sit down until it passes.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. It feels like the minute I finish one feed, the next is due, or there’s laundry piled up, bottles to wash, and I’m running on empty. I’ll look at the mess and just… freeze, thinking I’ll never dig my way out. I manage the basics, but it’s like wading through thick mud all day.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Exactly. I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning—replaying every little thing I did wrong, worrying about tomorrow, listening for the baby even when she’s quiet. It takes me ages to drift off, and if I wake up I’m instantly wide-awake worrying again. Some nights I only get three broken hours.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day this week. I’ll be rocking the baby and tears just start rolling down my face, or I’ll stare out the window feeling this heavy sadness I can’t shake. It’s like a gray cloud that follows me even when nothing specific is wrong.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried maybe three or four times since last week. Once was because the baby wouldn’t latch and I felt useless, another time I just spilled some formula and burst into tears. It’s like the smallest thing tips me over and I can’t stop the waterworks.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—I haven’t had any thoughts like that. I feel low, but I’ve never wanted to hurt myself. I just want to feel better so I can be the mom my baby needs.

You've shared that the past week has felt overwhelmingly heavy-daily <sym>sadness</sym>, frequent <sym>tears</sym>, and little <sym>joy</sym> even when you know something should be funny. You described <sym>guilt</sm> that pounces over tiny mishaps, <sym>panic</sym> that arrives without warning, and nights spent <sym>unable to sleep</sym> while your mind races with worries about your baby's safety. Yet you clearly love your little one and want to feel better so you can be the mom you hope to be.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 24, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient reports markedly reduced enjoyment and fleeting laughter, matching 'Definitely not so much now</sym>, <sym>Patient reports total loss of anticipatory pleasure, describing even simple past enjoyments as chores with "no spark," matching "Hardly at all."</sym>, <sym>Patient reports frequent, intense self-blame for minor incidents, describing guilt as automatic and disproportionate, aligning with "Yes, most of the time."</sym>, <sym>Patient describes daily, intrusive, catastrophic worries without basis—classic "very often" pattern</sym>, <sym>"Yes, quite a lot"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes frequent daily overwhelm and difficulty coping, matching "sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes nightly sleep disruption with racing thoughts, hypervigilance, and fragmented sleep, matching "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes daily, pervasive sadness with uncontrollable tears and persistent heaviness, aligning with "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports multiple crying episodes triggered by minor stressors, matching "Yes, quite often"</sym>)
**Reasoning:** Score of 24 exceeds the 14-point cutoff indicating high likelihood of <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. Patient meets core criteria: depressed mood most of the day, diminished interest (<sym>anhedonia</sym>), self-reproach, and insomnia nearly every day for more than two weeks. Associated <sym>anxiety symptoms</sym> (racing heart, breathlessness, catastrophic worries) are common in postpartum presentations. <quote>I just want to feel better so I can be the mom my baby needs</quote> underscores distress and functional impact. No self-harm ideation (Q10 score 0) lowers acute risk but ongoing monitoring essential. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider</med> or <med>perinatal mental health specialist</med> within the next few days
2. Schedule formal diagnostic interview and consider standardized <med>PHQ-9</med> or <med>GAD-7</med> for baseline severity
3. Discuss evidence-based treatment options including <med>CBT</med>, peer support, and, if appropriate, <med>sertraline</med> compatible with breastfeeding
4. Encourage 20-30 minutes of daylight walking and acceptance of help with night feeds to improve <sym>sleep</sym>
5. Provide 24-h crisis line numbers and safety plan even though self-harm currently denied
6. Re-screen with EPDS in 2 weeks to track progress after intervention
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – EPDS equivalent  
Date: [today]

Patient: 2–3 wks post-delivery, primiparous, breastfeeding.

Symptom Endorsement  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, anhedonia (daily)  
- Excessive guilt / self-blame re: mothering competence  
- Marked anxiety (racing heart, “can’t catch breath,” catastrophic worries about infant safety)  
- Panic spells without precipitant (3× this week)  
- Initial & middle insomnia related to rumination, hyper-vigilance to infant  
- Overwhelmed / “frozen,” difficulty completing routine tasks  
- Crying spells triggered by minor incidents (spilled milk, latch difficulty)  

Pattern  
Symptoms present most days for ≥ 2 wks, causing subjective impairment in functioning; no prior psych history reported.

Safety  
Denies any thoughts of self-harm or harm to infant (Q10 negative); nevertheless, ongoing assessment warranted given moderate-severe mood and anxiety burden.

Screening Impression  
High likelihood of major postpartum depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; meets cutoff for further evaluation. Recommend formal diagnostic interview, depression/anxiety measures, psycho-education, support mobilization, and discussion of treatment options.
